subject: VegaCart throughput regression - RCA, exec commitments, and remediation follow-through
messages:
From: Lara Coleman <lara.coleman@vegacart.com>
To: support@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: Michael Ruiz <m.ruiz@vegacart.com>, ops@vegacart.com
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden throughput drop on production (US-west) — urgent

Hi team,

We started seeing a sharp drop in throughput for our checkout route around 08:45 PDT this morning. Requests are queuing and average latency has spiked to ~3.2s for tokenized generation calls; error rate also increased briefly. Our customers (payments flow) were impacted for about 18 minutes before traffic normalized.

Can you confirm root cause and next steps? VegaCart is under a weekend promotion and our execs want an internal readout plus a clear remediation timeline.

Attached are our synthetic monitor screenshots and a short trace from our side.

Thanks,
Lara Coleman
Director, Platform Engineering
VegaCart
[Attachment: vegacart-monitor-20270720.png (image/png)]

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Lara Coleman <lara.coleman@vegacart.com>, Michael Ruiz <m.ruiz@vegacart.com>, ops@vegacart.com

Subject: Re: Sudden throughput drop on production (US-west) — urgent

Hi Lara / Michael — thanks for the heads up and the traces. I’ve opened an incident bridge and looped in the on-call infra team. We’re treating this as a P2 with exec visibility; I’ll keep you posted with updates every 30 minutes until we have a mitigation.

Immediate next steps we’re taking internally:
- triage traces + kernel-level metrics (KV cache pressure, batching windows)
- confirm whether a routing fallback triggered
- collect per-model queue depths and GPU utilization

Marissa / Kim / Jonas: please join the bridge if available (details in calendar invite).

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: bridge-ics.ics (text/calendar)]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: VegaCart incident triage notes

Team — quick notes from the bridge (10:00-10:40):
- Symptom: throughput drop + short burst of 5xxs between 08:45–09:03 PDT.
- Immediate cause: model shard rebalancing during autoscaling where one pool entered a degraded state; during rebalance we saw a KV cache miss spike which increased per-request CPU path and caused queuing.
- Contributing factors: (a) autoscaler settings allow concurrent scale operations for pools serving same model family; (b) a recent kernel update (rolled 2027-07-10) changed a batching heuristic under specific sequence-length distributions; (c) VegaCart’s traffic pattern (promo burst) created an atypical sequence-length tail.

Actions committed on bridge:
1) rollback kernel heuristic to previous stable commit (ops) — ETA 1h (done at 11:05).
2) apply temporary routing rule to route VegaCart traffic to dedicated pool without rebalance (infra) — ETA 25m (done at 10:55).
3) run KV cache warmup and increase cache retention for that pool (runtime team) — ETA 2h.
4) customer-facing RCA draft and exec note (CS) — Vanessa to lead.

I captured relevant logs and exported a trace snippet (attached). I’ll assemble a short RCA draft for Vanessa.

—Marissa
[Attachment: service-trace-snippet.txt (text/plain)]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Draft RCA + timeline (v1)

Vanessa — attaching an internal RCA v1 and a proposed mitigation timeline. Highlights:
- Root cause: concurrent autoscale + recent batching heuristic produced KV cache churn and CPU-side slow-paths.
- Impact window: 08:45–09:03 PDT; peak error rate 6.8% on the checkout route; estimated 18% drop in throughput for that route at peak.
- Remediations: rollback (complete), routing isolation (complete), KV cache adjustments (in progress), more conservative autoscaler guardrails (proposal).
- Exec asks for Redwood: commit to formalizing autoscaler guardrails, add an automated pre-deploy smoke that simulates sequence-length tail, and provide a 30/60/90 day remediation plan.

Attachments: vega_rca_v1.pdf, mitigation-timeline.xlsx

Let me know what to include in the customer-facing note; I flagged the kernel change rather than detailed internal sharding behavior.

-Marissa
[Attachment: vega_rca_v1.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Lara Coleman <lara.coleman@vegacart.com>, Michael Ruiz <m.ruiz@vegacart.com>, ops@vegacart.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, leadership@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-incident RCA and remediation commitments for VegaCart (summary)

Hi Lara / Michael — thank you again for patience while we investigated. Attached is our RCA summary and the remediation timeline; below are the key points and concrete commitments from Redwood: 

Summary:
- What happened: concurrent autoscaling + a recent batching heuristic produced KV cache churn which temporarily increased CPU-side latency and caused request queuing in one serving pool.
- Impact: 08:45–09:03 PDT on 2027-07-20. Peak error rate 6.8% for the checkout route; throughput degraded ~18% for the impacted window.

Redwood commitments (actionable, with owners & ETA):
1) Immediate rollback of heuristic (complete) — Owner: infra, Completed: 2027-07-20 11:05 PDT.
2) Routing isolation to dedicated pool (complete) — Owner: infra, Completed: 2027-07-20 10:55 PDT.
3) KV cache warmup and retention increase (in progress) — Owner: runtime team, ETA: 2027-07-22 EOD.
4) Autoscaler guardrails proposal (design + code) — Owner: infra + runtime, ETA: 2027-07-29.
5) Deployment smoke test for sequence-length tail (automation) — Owner: SRE, ETA: 2027-08-15.
6) Exec readout & one-page postmortem for VegaCart leadership — Owner: Vanessa, ETA: 2027-07-22.

Attachments: vega_rca_v1.pdf (detailed RCA), mitigation-timeline.xlsx (task schedule). We have also uploaded supporting traces to the Drive link included below.

We know this was time-sensitive for your promotion traffic — we’ll confirm when KV warmup completes and send a short verification test from our synthetic monitors. If you want an on-call replay session this week, we can schedule it.

Apologies again for the disruption. We’re treating the autoscaler guardrails as a priority to avoid recurrence and will include you in validation.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: mitigation-timeline.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]
